explanation: Sort intervals by start. Merge each interval into the last result when their closed ranges touch or overlap; otherwise start a new result range.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) time for n intervals. Sorting n intervals dominates the linear merge scan.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary and output space. The sorted sequence and independent result rows each require O(n) storage.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Sort by the left endpoint so a later interval cannot overlap any completed output range except the last one. Merging overlapping or touching ranges preserves their union; starting a new range when separated preserves disjointness. The final output is therefore exactly the input union.
walkthrough: For [[5,9],[1,3],[3,6],[12,14]], sorting starts with [1,3]. Touching [3,6] extends it to [1,6], then [5,9] extends it to [1,9]. The separated [12,14] remains, giving [[1,9],[12,14]].
edgeCases: Nested intervals do not shorten an existing merged range.
Equal endpoints are included and merge when they touch.
